channel.title: DevPulse · Web
channel.description: Daily web stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Chrome 155 ships JPEG XL decoding with a Rust implementation
item.description: Chrome 155 adds JPEG XL decoding; the announcement cites 30–50% better compression than JPEG and describes a Rust decoder and performance work. Browser support and decoder safety matter to teams delivering image-heavy web products.

item.title: A browser app finds routes that trade distance for less climbing in San Francisco
item.description: The app computes routes over 160,000 street segments using lidar elevation and OpenStreetMap data, with a slider for trading distance against climbing. It is a useful example of substantial route computation and data working in the browser.

item.title: Web developers still have reasons to build beyond browser APIs
item.description: The essay weighs “use the platform” against the history of browser gaps, when libraries such as jQuery supplied features browsers had yet to implement. It offers useful context for choosing native APIs versus dependencies, though its focus is web development.

item.title: Bez generates a browser engine from specifications and tests
item.description: Bez proposes generating browser engines from specifications, candidate implementations, comparisons with shipping browsers and Web Platform Tests; it also describes builds limited to features a site uses. The approach could change the cost and footprint of embedding web rendering, though the excerpt gives no results.

item.title: SvelteKit 3 adds type-safety improvements and a migration command
item.description: SvelteKit 3 moves configuration to Vite, changes the library alias, and offers a migration command that generates a TODO list for remaining work. The release is relevant to frontend teams planning framework upgrades.

item.title: Vinext 1.0 makes Next.js apps portable across web platforms
item.description: Vinext 1.0 adds compatibility and caching improvements and supports deploying Pages or App Router apps to Workers, Netlify, and AWS Lambda. Engineers maintaining Next.js apps can weigh a path to broader deployment portability.

item.title: EmDash 1.0 pairs a production CMS with a decentralized plugin registry
item.description: EmDash 1.0 combines Astro-based site building and editorial workflows with API, CLI, and MCP access for agents; its plugin registry lets developers publish without relying on a central marketplace. It is a concrete look at how a web product can expose agent interfaces while handling extensions.

item.title: A cross-platform Markdown editor keeps notes as plain files
item.description: The editor renders Markdown in place, stores notes as plain files, keeps version history, and syncs shared notes peer to peer over WebRTC. Its custom contenteditable implementation and cross-platform constraints offer useful product-engineering detail.
